_comment: AI neural network and PPO hyperparameters. All tunable constants live here, not hardcoded - mirrors physics.json/attributes.json pattern.

logging._comment_consistency_interval_s: How often the match logger emits a 'consistency' snapshot entry when no other events have fired (seconds of sim time).

eval._comment: Seeded evaluation, shared by PPOTrainer._eval_vs_rules() (pre-training + every rollout) and evaluate.py -- see ai/eval/seeded_eval.py. eval_n_seeds fixed scenario seeds starting at eval_seed_base are reused identically every eval call, so results are comparable across an entire run instead of noise from a fresh random scenario draw each time. eval_repeats_per_seed re-runs each seed that many times (averaged into the same aggregate stats) to reduce residual match-physics/PPO-sampling noise without growing the scenario set. eval_n_parallel_workers >1 spawns that many subprocesses (mirrors ppo.n_parallel_envs); this does NOT seed PPO training itself, only evaluation call sites.

observation._comment_max_task_ids: Width of the GlobalFeatures task-id one-hot (scaffolding, see ai/knowledge.md 'Task-id: scaffolded, not yet load-bearing'). Must match schema.py's MAX_TASK_IDS.
observation._comment_sim_dt_s: Physics tick size. Default 0.0333 (30Hz). Increase for faster training: 0.05=20Hz (~1.5x), 0.067=15Hz (~2x). UI ignores this and always uses 30Hz.
observation._comment_ball_spin_norm_max_rad_s: Shared between two systems: (1) ai/obs/encoder.py's live-match spin normalization scale, and (2) physics_pretrain.ball's sampling-range upper bound for _sample_spin (ball_episode_gen.py) -- how strong a spin CAN be drawn for a synthetic episode. It is NOT physics_pretrain's dataset normalization divisor -- that's the separate, deliberately hardcoded BALL_SPIN_NORM_DIVISOR_RAD_S (=30.0) constant in ball_episode_gen.py, chosen so widening this sampling range doesn't retroactively change how already-generated dataset shards encode spin (ball_dataset.generate_dataset APPENDS to existing shards rather than overwriting, so a drifting divisor would silently mix incompatible normalizations across shards). If you raise this value to get stronger training-signal spin, note ai/ppo/bc.py has its own hardcoded `spin_norm_max = 30.0  # matches ai_config.json obs['ball_spin_norm_max_rad_s']` for its kick_spin BC loss -- that comment goes stale (and BC's spin loss normalization silently diverges from the live encoder's) unless updated by hand alongside this value.
observation._comment_time: Use log1p normalization for time_remaining to spread out the low end (see ai_design_doc.md section 7.5)

network._comment_inter_player_attn_heads: Heads for the inter-player self-attention pass that runs over other-player embeddings BEFORE the main query step. Divisors of entity_embed_dim (45): 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45. 0 = disabled. No-op in 1v1; becomes useful for 2v2+ where player-player relational context matters.
network._comment_share_entity_encoder: If true, ExecutionNetwork reuses DecisionNetwork's entity_encoder, ball_mlp, and global_mlp (same nn.Module objects, shared weights + shared gradient). Halves encoder computation per decision tick. Set false to give each network fully independent encoders.
network._comment_exec_trunk_hidden: Trunk hidden dim for the main policy ExecutionNetwork. null = fall back to trunk_hidden. Set a smaller int (e.g. 96) to reduce execution network capacity and rely more on the decision latent.
network._comment_value_net_trunk_hidden: Optional override for trunk_hidden used ONLY by the dedicated separate value network (trainer.value_net, see ppo.__init__ 'separate_value_net' / CLI --separate-value-net). null (default) = same size as the main trunk_hidden above. Set an int (e.g. 96 for a smaller/cheaper critic, or 384 for a bigger one) to size the standalone critic's trunk independently of the shared policy trunk -- has NO effect at all when --separate-value-net is not passed (the main execution_net always uses trunk_hidden).
network._comment_value_hidden_dim: Hidden layer size for value_head (critic). 0 = old behaviour, a single Linear(trunk_hidden+value_extra_hidden, 1) with no nonlinearity. >0 inserts one Linear+ReLU hidden layer before the final scalar output, giving the critic its own nonlinear capacity instead of relying purely on a linear readout of the shared (policy) trunk. Try 32-128; raise if value RMSE plateaus well above 0 while train loss for the policy looks fine.
network._comment_value_dropout: Dropout probability applied ONLY inside value_head (ExecutionNetwork), immediately before each Linear layer -- never touches the shared trunk `h` that also feeds the policy/motor heads, so it cannot destabilise action distributions. 0.0 (default) = disabled. Motivated by pretrain_value() overfitting hard on a small offline rollout (train loss falling steadily while val loss rises after ~epoch 4-5, see ai_trainer_knowledge.md 'value_head overfitting'). Try 0.1-0.3. Note: nn.Dropout auto-disables under .eval() but PPO rollout action-sampling does NOT call .eval() on execution_net, so this also lightly perturbs the value estimate used for GAE bootstrapping during rollout collection -- harmless (value isn't used to pick actions) but worth knowing if you see val= jitter increase after enabling.
network._comment: Shared-trunk actor/critic (Option A from section 9.4). Switch to separate trunk if value loss destabilises policy.

ppo._comment_gamma: Discount factor: how much future rewards are worth vs immediate ones. Think of it as 'I care about a reward in N steps at gamma^N of its face value'. 0.99 = reward 100 steps away is worth 37% of today's reward. 0.995 = same reward is still worth 61%. Typical range: 0.95–0.999. We use 0.995 because episodes are long (~120s, ~170 decision steps) and the terminal reward (+5) is the main signal — too low and the agent gives up on distant goals, too high and variance explodes. Raise toward 0.999 if the agent seems short-sighted; lower toward 0.99 if training is unstable.
ppo._comment_lam: GAE lambda: controls the bias/variance tradeoff in advantage estimation. lam=1.0 is pure Monte Carlo (low bias, high variance — noisy but unbiased). lam=0.0 is pure TD(0) (high bias, low variance — smooth but wrong). Typical range: 0.9–0.99. We use 0.97 as a standard middle ground. Lower (e.g. 0.9) if gradients are noisy and training oscillates; raise (e.g. 0.99) if the agent seems to discount future steps too aggressively.
ppo._comment_clip_range: PPO clipping: the policy ratio (new_prob / old_prob) is clamped to [1-clip, 1+clip] = [0.95, 1.05] here. This stops a single update from changing the policy too drastically — the gradient is zeroed for any sample where the ratio goes outside the band. Typical value is 0.2; we use 0.05 (very conservative) because the KL was spiking to 0.4+ with 0.1, causing early-stop after just 2 minibatches. Lower clip = more conservative updates, more minibatches get through. If you see 25+ minibatches per rollout and training is slow, try raising to 0.1.
ppo._comment_vf_coef: Value function loss coefficient: scales how hard the critic trains relative to the actor. total_loss = policy_loss + vf_coef*value_loss - ent_coef*entropy. Typical: 0.5. Raise if the value estimates are wildly off (large RMSE vs returns std); lower if value gradients seem to destabilise the policy (rare).
ppo._comment_ent_coef: Legacy constant entropy coefficient -- only used as the DEFAULT for ent_coef_start below when that key is absent. total_loss = policy_loss + vf_coef*value_loss - ent_coef*entropy, so this is a FIXED per-step reward for being uncertain, with no self-limiting mechanism: the policy-gradient term's opposing pull shrinks as advantages shrink over training, but a constant ent_coef's pull does not, so entropy can win by default late in training even at a small value. Set ent_coef_start/end/anneal_fraction below to anneal instead of relying on this constant. See ai_trainer_knowledge.md 'Reading the training log' entropy discussion (run110 case study: entropy climbed monotonically for all 6M steps at a fixed ent_coef, eventually costing ~10 points of win-rate via noisier kick/tackle/braking execution once it crossed roughly the 4.4-4.6 nats range).
ppo._comment_ent_coef_anneal: Linear anneal of the entropy coefficient from ent_coef_start to ent_coef_end, reaching ent_coef_end by ent_coef_anneal_fraction of total_steps and holding flat after (same shape as bc.aux_coeff_start/end/anneal_fraction). Defaults to a no-op (constant at ent_coef_start, itself defaulting to the legacy ent_coef above) when these three keys are absent, so existing configs/checkpoints are unaffected until set explicitly. Values here are a starting guess, not tuned: end is a small nonzero floor (not 0) so some exploration persists. Use the per-rollout '[per-head entropy]' log line and the 'value' line's |adv| figure to check whether entropy is still rising / whether |adv| has bottomed out, and adjust the endpoint accordingly rather than trusting these numbers blindly -- especially now that ent_dir_weight no longer dampens the direction heads' contribution to the PPO ratio (see _comment_ent_dir_weight), which changes how much of the aggregate entropy trend those heads are likely to drive.
ppo._comment_max_grad_norm: Gradient clipping: if the total gradient vector has magnitude > this, all gradients are scaled down proportionally. Acts as a safety valve against catastrophic updates from rare high-loss samples. 0.5 is standard for PPO. Raise to 1.0 if gradients feel too constrained (loss barely moves per step); lower to 0.3 if you see sudden policy collapses. Check the 'g=' value in the per-rollout log — if it's consistently hitting 0.5 exactly, you're clipping every update. Does NOT apply to the direction-head params (move_direction/kick_direction weights + move_dir_log_std/kick_dir_log_std) when direction_max_grad_norm below is set — those get their own isolated clip_grad_norm_() call.
ppo._comment_direction_max_grad_norm: Optional separate gradient-norm clip applied ONLY to the direction-head params (move_direction/kick_direction Linear weights + move_dir_log_std/kick_dir_log_std). null (default) = fall back to max_grad_norm, i.e. direction params are clipped together with everything else in one combined-norm group (prior behaviour). Set a float to isolate direction gradients into their own clip so a single outlier sample's large move_dir/kick_dir gradient can no longer force a proportional shrink of the rest of the network's gradient in the same step (and vice versa — a calm direction gradient no longer 'borrows' clip headroom from a genuinely large gradient elsewhere). See ai_trainer_knowledge.md 'grad norm clipping' discussion for the rationale; this directly bounds how far move_direction's predicted mean can move per gradient step, which is the root cause of the large angular_diff KL outliers seen in training logs. Raised from 0.015 to 0.3 after removing ent_dir_weight's scaling from the direction heads' log_prob/PPO-ratio computation (ent_dir_weight now only scales the entropy bonus, see _comment_ent_dir_weight) -- that scaling was compressing the true ratio contribution from these heads by ~1/ent_dir_weight before this change, so real gradients reaching these params are now far larger than the old 0.015 ceiling was calibrated for. 0.3 is an informed starting guess (well under the main max_grad_norm=0.4, still isolated in its own clip group), NOT a tuned value -- watch the '[grad clip] direction: N/M steps clipped (%) pre-clip norm mean=X max=Y' log line on the first couple of rollouts after this change: raise further if it's clipping >50% of steps at max=Y >> limit (signal still being choked), lower if it's rarely engaging at all and direction KL/ratio outliers reappear.
ppo._comment_learning_rate: Step size for Adam optimiser. Typical PPO LR is 3e-4, but we use 5e-6 because (a) augmentation multiplies the effective batch by 12x meaning each gradient step sees more signal, and (b) the BC-pretrained policy is already near a good point so large steps would destroy it. Raise to 1e-5 if training feels too slow; lower to 1e-6 if the policy collapses after pretraining. Does NOT apply to the direction-head params when direction_learning_rate below is set — those get their own Adam param group/LR.
ppo._comment_direction_learning_rate: Optional separate Adam LR for the direction-head param group (move_direction/kick_direction weights + move_dir_log_std/kick_dir_log_std). null (default) = fall back to learning_rate, i.e. direction params share the main 'policy' param group's LR (prior behaviour). Set a float smaller than learning_rate to directly shrink how much move_direction's predicted mean can move per gradient step, independent of the rest of the policy — complementary to direction_max_grad_norm (LR scales the step size AFTER grad-norm clipping bounds the raw gradient magnitude).
ppo._comment_value_learning_rate: Separate, much higher LR for the value_head (+ value_extra_mlp) param group only — the policy LR above is deliberately tiny to protect the BC-primed policy, but sharing it with the critic starves value learning: the per-minibatch KL early-stop (see target_kl) is based on policy KL and often cuts a rollout's gradient steps to 1-5, which was leaving the value head unable to track the shifting self-play return distribution (normalized value loss stuck >1.0 post-PPO despite a well-converged pretrain). Comparable in scale to value_pretrain_lr/demo_value_pretrain_lr. Falls back to `learning_rate` if absent.
ppo._comment_value_weight_decay: Adam weight_decay (L2) applied ONLY to the value param group ('value_head'/'value_ai_type_channel' params, or trainer.value_net's optimizer when --separate-value-net) during PPO. 0.0 (default) = disabled, matching prior behaviour. Each rollout's data is used for only ppo.n_epochs passes and the return distribution keeps shifting under self-play, so overfitting-to-one-batch is less of a risk here than in bc.value_pretrain_weight_decay's offline setting -- this is mainly cheap insurance for generalisation across the whole run. Try 1e-4 to 1e-3.
ppo._comment_value_only_continuation_epochs: Epoch budget for the value-only continuation loop that runs after the policy's per-minibatch KL early-stop cuts the main epoch loop short (see target_kl) — trains ONLY the value_head/value_extra_mlp param group (no policy forward/backward, so no further KL risk) for up to this many additional passes over the same rollout batch. Defaults to n_epochs if absent (previous, implicit behaviour was to reuse n_epochs unconditionally). Raise if 'val=' stays high despite frequent early-stops; lower if you're worried about overfitting the critic to a single stale rollout batch (see ai/knowledge.md).
ppo._comment_target_kl: Per-minibatch early-stop threshold. KL divergence measures how much the policy distribution has changed since the rollout was collected — KL=0 means no change, KL=0.4 means fairly significant shift. When any minibatch's KL exceeds this, the entire epoch loop stops early. Typical value is 0.01–0.05; we use 0.4 (very permissive) because we want to see how many minibatches naturally get through. The real constraint is clip_range=0.05. LOWER this (e.g. 0.1) to make early-stop fire sooner and protect the policy more aggressively — you'll see fewer minibatches per rollout but more stable training. RAISE it if you want to see the full picture of how the policy changes per rollout.
ppo._comment_n_parallel_envs: Number of worker PROCESSES running independent ScenarioEnv copies for on-policy rollout collection. 1 (default) = current single-process behaviour, no subprocess overhead. >1 spawns that many subprocesses (see ai/ppo/rollout_worker.py), each with its own env + local policy copy, weight-synced from the main process before every rollout. Used by BOTH: (1) the main PPO training loop (rollout_steps split evenly across workers), and (2) pretrain_value()'s/pretrain_combined()'s Phase 2/3 value-warm-up rollout collection (its own n_steps split the same way) -- see ai_trainer_knowledge.md 'Parallel rollout collection'. Physics stepping is pure-Python/CPU-bound (GIL-limited under threads), so this only helps via real OS processes. Does NOT affect BC pre-training's dataset epochs or the PPO/value gradient updates themselves -- those stay single-process.
ppo._comment_worker_torch_threads: torch.set_num_threads() inside each rollout worker process (see n_parallel_envs). Each worker only ever does batch-of-1 CPU forward passes, so >1 thread just adds intra-process contention across N worker processes competing for the same cores; 1 (default) is correct almost always.
ppo._comment_main_process_torch_threads: torch.set_num_threads() in the main process for train.py and debug_value_network.py -- BC pre-training and the PPO/value gradient update run small-batch ops here, unrelated to worker_torch_threads/n_parallel_envs above. Unlike batch-of-1 rollout workers, PyTorch's all-cores default measurably slows these down (thread sync overhead per op exceeds the compute saved on small batches/models) -- 4 was found empirically faster than both 1 and os.cpu_count(). Re-benchmark if the model or batch size changes materially.
ppo._comment_dir_log_std_headroom: dir_log_std_max raised from -0.85 to -0.5 (sigma ~24.5 deg -> ~35 deg ceiling) because dir_log_std_init=-0.9 (sigma~23.3 deg) sat almost AT the old -0.85 ceiling, leaving move_dir_log_std essentially no room to grow -- the clamp zeroes gradient once the raw parameter drifts past its bound, so an init this close to the ceiling could get stuck unresponsive immediately. Widened as part of the KL-explosion fix (see ai_trainer_knowledge.md): removing ent_dir_weight's ratio dampening meant real gradient reaches move_dir/move_dir_log_std for the first time, and a wider sigma directly shrinks KL~=(delta_mu)^2/(2*sigma^2) for the same angular drift.
ppo._comment_dir_log_std_reg: Explicit L2 restoring force pulling move_dir_log_std toward dir_log_std_target and kick_dir_log_std toward kick_dir_log_std_target. move_* keys fall back to dir_log_std_* for backward compat. Without this, ent_dir_weight's entropy bonus only ever inflates log_std with nothing pulling it back. 0.0 = disabled. Try 0.01-0.1.
ppo._comment_kick_power_spin_log_std_init: Initial log_std for the kick_power (SquashedNormalHead, sigmoid-squashed scalar in [0,1]) and kick_spin (plain unsquashed 3D Normal -- kick_spin has no bounded physical range wired up yet, it's still disabled at the apply_nn_action.py chokepoint per agent_plans/spin_implementation_plan.md) heads. Both were previously applied fully deterministically (raw mean only, no sampling/log_prob/entropy at all -- see plan doc section 6/1.3). 0.0 preserves the exact prior nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(...)) init now that these are actually read. This is a scoped fix for the missing-exploration bug only -- NOT the fuller spin-axis/magnitude redesign discussed in the plan doc, which is deferred.
ppo._comment_ent_dir_weight: Weight applied to continuous direction heads (move_dir, kick_dir) in the ENTROPY BONUS ONLY (_compute_entropy). The direction heads output a Gaussian distribution; their raw entropy is much larger in scale than a Bernoulli head. 1.0 = equal weight = direction entropy dominates the bonus and the Bernoulli heads (shoot, sprint etc.) get almost no exploration pressure. 0.05 = direction entropy contributes only 5% — Bernoulli heads drive exploration. Lower toward 0.01 if the agent spins randomly (too much directional noise); raise toward 0.2 if kicks/passes cluster on one angle. Previously this ALSO scaled the direction heads' log_prob contribution to the actual PPO importance ratio (_compute_log_prob/_recompute_log_prob/_per_head_new_log_probs) -- that coupling was removed: a small ent_dir_weight was silently compressing the TRUE probability ratio for these heads toward 1.0 (ratio_true^ent_dir_weight), which both defeated PPO's clip/KL trust-region protection for direction heads specifically (large true drift never triggered clipping or early-stop) AND attenuated the real policy-gradient signal reaching them by the same factor -- compounding with (not replaced by) direction_learning_rate/direction_max_grad_norm below, which are the correct, non-distorting levers for controlling how fast/far direction heads move. See ai_trainer_knowledge.md's entropy/direction-heads discussion. kick_spin_axis reuses this same weight (architecturally identical to move_dir/kick_dir -- a DirectionHead) rather than getting its own key.
ppo._comment_ent_kick_power_spin_weight: Entropy bonus weight for the kick_power (SquashedNormalHead) and kick_spin (plain 3D Normal) heads, both E[kick active]-weighted -- matching how sprint/move_dir/kick_dir are weighted by their own parent-active probability in _compute_entropy. Separate from ent_dir_weight since neither is a DirectionHead (unit-vector Gaussian).
ppo._comment_augment: Slot permutations per geometric flip variant. Total batch multiplier = N_FLIP_VARIANTS(2) * n. Use 1 for 2x (flip_y only), 3 for 6x, 0 to disable. flip_x is no longer part of this random augmentation -- it's now a permanent canonical-AI-frame transform, see ai/obs/canonical.py. See ai/obs/augment.py.
ppo._comment_rollout_eval: Number of trials run vs rules-based AI after each PPO rollout update. Set to 0 to disable the per-rollout eval entirely.
ppo._comment: Standard PPO defaults from CleanRL-style reference implementations. Tune empirically.

curriculum._comment_todo: TODO: implement and wire up: rng_reduction_start/end (randomisation annealing over training), pitch_standard_fraction (fraction of episodes on standard pitch), pitch_min_scale / goal_min_scale (curriculum pitch scaling). Currently not read by any code.
curriculum._comment_phase1_opponent: phase1 training opponent split expressed as unnormalized ratios (normalized at read time). Neural remainder is used during PPO training as a secondary player. During demo recording, neural falls back to Phase1RulesAI — no neural opponent exists at demo time. Immobile-opponent episodes are excluded from BC training by DemonstrationDataset.valid_indices().
curriculum._comment_secondary_weight: Importance weight applied to secondary (opponent) player transitions in the PPO loss. 1.0 = equal weight, 0.5 = half weight, 0.0 = ignore secondary transitions.

bc._comment: Behavioural cloning from rules-based AI. Set pretrain_steps=0 to skip pre-training. Set aux_coeff_start=0.0 to disable the PPO auxiliary BC loss.
bc._comment_label_smoothing: Label smoothing for BC Bernoulli targets before BCE: target = target*(1-eps) + 0.5*eps. dec_label_smoothing applies to the 7 decision heads (shoot/pass/move/tackle/gp_extra/mark/hold); exec_label_smoothing applies to the 4 execution Bernoulli heads (exec_move, sprint, kick_this_tick, tackle_attempt). 0.0 = disabled (default). Try 0.02-0.05 if BC-primed heads become overconfident and cause PPO's per-minibatch KL early-stop to fire on minibatch 0 of the first rollout (see ai_trainer_knowledge.md / training log analysis) — exec_move/sprint sitting at confident post-BC probabilities makes Bernoulli KL highly nonlinear, so even a tiny first gradient step overshoots target_kl.
bc._comment_pos_weight: null = auto-compute from the training dataset at load time via DemonstrationDataset.compute_pos_weights() (recommended). Set a float to override. pos_weight_max caps the auto-computed inverse-frequency ratio (e.g. tackle_attempt was hitting ~134.5) before use — null = uncapped. Only applies to the auto-computed path; has no effect when pos_weight_kick/pos_weight_tackle_attempt are set explicitly.
bc._comment_max_grad_norm: Grad-norm clip for BC pretrain's optimizers (Phase 0 demo_opt, Phase 1 bc_opt, Phase 4 repair_opt). Absent from config = fall back to ppo.max_grad_norm (prior behaviour, shares PPO's very conservative clip). Set a float here to give BC pretrain its own cap instead -- BC uses a much higher LR (bc_learning_rate) and full supervised minibatch descent with no PPO trust-region concept, so PPO's tight clip can suppress useful large early-training corrections. Set explicitly to null (as here) to disable clipping entirely during BC.
bc._comment_downsample: Gentle per-epoch downsampling of 'trivial' BC movement rows (see DemonstrationDataset._compute_trivial_mask). frac_default is used for epochs < epoch_threshold, frac_high_epoch afterward. Freshly re-rolled every epoch, never a fixed one-time filter. downsample_trivial_exclude_radius_steps also protects rows near a sprint/exec_move speedMode change, not just kick_this_tick/tackle_attempt.
bc._comment_aux: aux_coeff ('other'), kick_aux_coeff ('kick'), and tackle_aux_coeff ('tackle') each anneal linearly from their own start to end, sharing aux_coeff_anneal_fraction of training as the anneal duration (e.g. 0.3 = all three done by 30% of steps). Only used by the online BC-aux-during-PPO term in PPOTrainer._ppo_update() (Mode 3) -- the offline pretraining/repair BC passes in pretrain_combined() still use the single combined loss, unaffected by this split. The BC loss (bc_loss_from_tensor() in bc.py, split_kick=True, split_tackle=True) covers EVERYTHING: all 7 decision Bernoullis, move_region_center MSE, exec_move/sprint Bernoullis, and move_direction cosine are scaled by aux_coeff ('other' group); kick_this_tick Bernoulli, kick_direction cosine, kick_power MSE, and kick_spin MSE (kick_spin's own PPO sampling is frozen as of 2026-08-17, see agent_plans/spin_implementation_plan.md section 0 -- its BC term still computes and is included in the kick group for consistency, but is zero-gradient until unfrozen) are scaled by kick_aux_coeff ('kick' group); tackle_attempt Bernoulli alone is scaled by tackle_aux_coeff ('tackle' group). Set aux_coeff_start/end=0.0 and kick_aux_coeff_start/end=1.0 (say) to train on kicking only for a round, independent of everything else -- same idea for tackle_aux_coeff.
bc._comment_bc_pretrain_early_stop: Episode-level 85/15 train/val split + early stop for pretrain_combined()'s main BC epoch loop, mirroring value_pretrain_early_stop_patience/min_delta below. patience=0 (default) = disabled (no split computed, no early stop -- matches prior behaviour of training BC blind on the full dataset for exactly bc_pretrain_epochs). Set e.g. 3-5 to enable: patience = consecutive non-improving epochs allowed before stopping and restoring best-val weights; min_delta = minimum val BC-loss decrease to count as improvement. See 'BC val=' log line when enabled.
bc._comment_dec_exec_weight: Relative weight of decision-network vs execution-network losses in BC (pretrain and PPO aux annealing). dec=1.0/exec=1.0 = equal. Raise bc_exec_weight to push execution network (sprint, direction, tackle) harder; lower to let it drift more freely under RL.
bc._comment_combined_pretrain_rollout_steps: Steps to collect for the on-policy rollout used by pretrain_combined()'s joint BC + value warm-up (its rollout_steps= argument) when an offline --bc-dataset is supplied. Completely separate variable from value_pretrain_steps below (the standalone pretrain_value() fallback used when no dataset is given) — the two are never meant to share a value, tune independently. Also independent of ppo.rollout_steps (the main PPO rollout buffer size).
bc._comment_value_pretrain_batch_size: Minibatch size for pretrain_value()'s value-only fitting loop (and Phase 0's demo-return value warm-up inside pretrain_combined()). Previously fell back silently to ppo.minibatch_size (12000) -- that size is tuned for PPO's clip/KL-early-stop dynamics, not for a plain supervised value-MSE regression, so it was an accidental coupling rather than a deliberate one. 512 gives noisier-but-more-frequent gradient steps, generally better for this kind of regression. Tune independently of ppo.minibatch_size and bc.bc_pretrain_batch_size.
bc._comment_value_pretrain_weight_decay: Adam weight_decay (L2) applied to pretrain_value()'s value optimizer(s) (execution_net.value_head-only optimizer, or trainer.value_net's optimizer when --separate-value-net). 0.0 (default) = disabled, matching prior behaviour. Motivated by train loss falling steadily (e.g. 0.41->0.30) while val loss RISES (0.46->0.57) over ~17 epochs before early-stop -- classic overfitting to a small, autocorrelated offline rollout reused for many epochs. Try 1e-4 to 1e-3; complements value_dropout (network.value_dropout) and the early-stop patience/min_delta below.
bc._comment_value_pretrain_early_stop: Value-pretrain-only early stop (see 'Value epoch' log lines): patience = consecutive non-improving epochs allowed before stopping; min_delta = minimum val-loss decrease to count as improvement. Raise patience if val loss looks noisy but still trending down slowly; raise min_delta to stop sooner on marginal improvements.
bc._comment_bc_train_value_only: When true, pretrain_combined() trains ONLY the value head(s): decision_net and execution_net's policy heads are frozen (requires_grad False) for the whole call, Phase 1's BC epoch loop and the BC repair epochs are both skipped entirely, and Phase 0 alone does the training -- correct under both separate_value_net=True/False since Phase 0 already routes to the right critic in each case. Use this to iterate on value-pretraining hyperparameters quickly against a large recorded/generated dataset without paying for policy backprop each pass.
bc._comment_bc_value_coef: Weight of the value MSE term added to the full BC pre-train loss in Phase 1 (both networks, demo returns). Separate from phase0_value_coef (decision-net-only Phase 0 warm-up). Falls back to demo_value_bc_coef if absent for backward compatibility.
bc._comment_phase0_value_coef: Weight of the value MSE term added to the decision-heads-only BC loss in Phase 0 (demo value pretrain). Phase 0 trains decision_net only (not execution_net), with NO frozen layers (unlike pretrain_value()'s standalone freezing) - one combined backward pass per minibatch: decision_bc_loss + phase0_value_coef * value_loss.
bc._comment_bc_only_continuation_epochs: Epoch budget for a BC-only continuation loop in PPOTrainer._ppo_update() that runs AFTER the value-only continuation (see ppo.value_only_continuation_epochs), when the policy's per-minibatch KL early-stop (ppo.target_kl) cuts the main epoch loop short. Runs bc_loss_from_tensor() + optimizer.step() on decision_net/execution_net params ONLY — no policy forward pass, no ratio/KL computed, so it cannot itself trigger further early-stops — using bc_only_continuation_coeff if set, otherwise falling back to the SAME annealed bc_coeff already computed for this rollout (see aux_coeff_start/end/anneal_fraction above). Rationale: BC's aux loss is normally applied inside the same KL-gated epoch/minibatch loop as the policy loss, so frequent early-stops were silently truncating BC's intended gradient budget every rollout (the value head already got its own dedicated continuation, BC did not). Default 0 = disabled (opt-in, new/experimental) — try 2-6 if BC influence looks weaker than aux_coeff implies (frequent early-stops + BC still not converging). Set 0 to disable without affecting the value-only continuation.
bc._comment_bc_only_continuation_coeff: Optional fixed coefficient for the bc-only continuation loop, decoupled from the annealed aux_coeff used by the in-epoch BC aux loss. null (default) = fall back to the annealed bc_coeff (prior behaviour) — this means setting aux_coeff_start/end to anneal to 0.0 also silently zeroes this continuation's effect even if bc_only_continuation_epochs > 0. Set a float (e.g. 0.3) to keep this continuation loop contributing a fixed BC gradient even after aux_coeff has annealed to 0, so BC no longer fights the main policy gradient during the KL-gated epoch loop but still nudges decision_net/execution_net toward demo behaviour using otherwise-unused post-early-stop gradient budget.
bc._comment_from_ckpt: These _from_ckpt variants are used instead of the defaults when --pretrain-from-checkpoint or --latest-pretrain is passed. Typically fewer epochs and lower aux coefficients since the policy is already near the demonstrations.
bc._comment_frozen_layers: Layers frozen (requires_grad=False) during value head warm-up. -1=all non-value layers (encoders + full trunk). 0=nothing frozen (gradients flow freely through trunk). 1=encoders only. 2=encoders + trunk layer 1. 3=encoders + full trunk (same as -1). Default -1 matches prior behaviour.
bc._comment_value: After BC pre-training, run value-only MSE warm-up so the critic is near the true return scale before PPO starts. Used by the standalone pretrain_value() fallback path (no --bc-dataset). value_pretrain_steps is independent of ppo.rollout_steps — 32768 ≈ 4× rollout buffer (~700 episodes). See ppo.combined_pretrain_rollout_steps for the equivalent sizing when pretrain_combined() is used instead. 15% of episodes held out as a val set; epoch loop stops early if val loss stagnates for 5 consecutive epochs. Set value_pretrain_steps=0 to skip.
bc._comment_demo_sample: Time between timed observation samples during demonstration recording. Kick2 and tackles are always recorded regardless.
bc._comment_demo_recording_n_processes: Number of worker PROCESSES for record_demonstrations.py (--n-processes overrides this). 1 (default) = current single-process behaviour. >1 splits --n-episodes evenly across that many subprocesses, each independently driving rules-based AI on both sides (no policy network, no weight sync needed -- much simpler than ppo.n_parallel_envs) and writing its own disjoint range of phase{N}_XXXX.npz files. Same GIL/physics rationale as ppo.n_parallel_envs -- see ai_trainer_knowledge.md 'Parallel rollout collection'.
bc._comment_demo_worker_torch_threads: torch.set_num_threads() per record_demonstrations.py worker (--worker-torch-threads overrides this). Only matters when --driver-checkpoint/--teacher-checkpoint load a network -- torch defaults to one thread per logical core, so with demo_recording_n_processes > 1 every worker left uncapped oversubscribes badly (N processes x full-core threading each). Keep at 1 unless you have a specific reason to raise it. Mirrors ppo.worker_torch_threads.

ema._comment: EMA smoothing for attack/defence weighting (section 2.7). alpha close to 1 = slow change, further from 1 = fast change.

phase1._comment_dist_shaping: Legacy positional retreat penalty (metres retreated × coef). Set to 0.0 to use heading_penalty_coef instead (recommended). Falls back to ball_distance_shaping if keys absent.
phase1._comment_ball_approach_speed_bonus: Squared closing-speed bonus: coef * max(0, prev_ball_dist - curr_ball_dist)^2 per step (0.0 disables). ball_approach_bonus/ball_retreat_penalty above are LINEAR in the per-step distance delta, which is potential-based and telescopes over an episode to coef*(start_dist-end_dist) — a player closing 10m in 2 fast steps and one closing the same 10m in 20 slow steps earn IDENTICAL total reward from those terms, so they cannot reward speed, only final position. Squaring breaks the telescoping (sum(x_i^2) >= (sum(x_i))^2/n, equality only when every step closes the same amount), so concentrating the same net distance into fewer/faster steps yields strictly more reward. Tune independently of ball_approach_bonus — a sensible starting point is roughly 2-5x ball_approach_bonus since per-step deltas are typically < 1.0m (squaring shrinks small values). See 'appr_sq' in the reward breakdown/training log.
phase1._comment_ball_retreat_speed_penalty: Squared retreating-speed penalty: coef * max(0, curr_ball_dist - prev_ball_dist)^2 per step, the symmetric-but-asymmetric-coefficient partner to ball_approach_speed_bonus (mirrors the existing ball_retreat_penalty > ball_approach_bonus asymmetry above). Falls back to ball_approach_speed_bonus's value if absent. Set higher than ball_approach_speed_bonus to penalize fast retreating more than fast approaching is rewarded. _delta = prev_ball_dist - curr_ball_dist is already the ball-relative closing speed (distance closed this step, i.e. player speed projected onto the direction to the ball) — not raw player speed — so this term only ever fires on genuine retreat along the ball axis.
phase1._comment_ball_approach_speed_reward_clam: Caps the EPISODE-CUMULATIVE positive ('approach') side of 'appr_sq' (via reward.cumulative_clamped_delta(), not a per-step clamp), same rationale as ball_progress_reward_clamp but applied to appr_sq instead of prog. null = uncapped default.
phase1._comment_ball_retreat_speed_reward_clamp: Caps the EPISODE-CUMULATIVE negative ('retreat') side of 'appr_sq' independently of ball_approach_speed_reward_clamp above — deliberately a SEPARATE bound (not one symmetric clamp) so it can match the already-independent ball_approach_speed_bonus/ball_retreat_speed_penalty coefficient asymmetry. null = uncapped default.
phase1._comment_heading_penalty: Penalty for moving away from the ball based on velocity direction vs ball direction. Formula: -coef * max(0, 1 - cos_sim)^exp. Only fires when |velocity| > min_speed_mps. cos_sim=1 (toward ball)=0 penalty; cos_sim=0 (perpendicular)=-coef; cos_sim=-1 (away)=-coef*2^exp. Set coef=0.0 to disable.
phase1._comment_stamina_penalty: End-of-episode penalty for stamina level: -coef * (1 - final_stamina). Range [0, coef]: 0 when full stamina, coef when completely exhausted. Applied once at episode termination only. Set to 0.0 to disable.
phase1._comment_ball_progress_reward_clamp: Caps the EPISODE-CUMULATIVE 'prog' total (via reward.cumulative_clamped_delta(), not a per-step clamp) so a long/wandering possession episode can't sum |prog| far past this value one small step at a time. null = uncapped.
phase1._comment_loss_terminal: Penalty applied when the opponent reaches the trainee's box with possession (trainee loses). Should be negative and less than box_possession_terminal in magnitude.
phase1._comment_loss_of_possession: Small penalty per step the trainee loses the ball to the opponent. Creates symmetric signal with gain_possession_bonus.
phase1._comment_timeout_penalty: Penalty if the episode times out (no resolution). Makes timeouts clearly worse than active play.
phase1._comment_proximity_bonus: On timeout only: bonus for how close the ball was to the opponent box. scale * max(0, 1 - dist/30m). Max = scale at box edge. Rewards making progress even when not winning.
phase1._comment_step_penalty: Flat penalty applied every decision step (including terminal). Encourages finishing quickly independent of episode outcome. Total episode cost = step_penalty * n_steps; with a 50s episode at 0.3s intervals that's ~167 steps, so step_penalty=0.01 costs ~1.67 over a full episode. Set to 0.0 to disable.
phase1._comment_speed_bonus: Bonus for finishing fast: scale * time_remaining_fraction. Max = scale (instant finish). Set to 0.0 to disable.

phase1_scenario._comment_opponent_dist: Constrain opponent placement distance from trainee. Both default to unconstrained. E.g. min=5, max=20 keeps opponent nearby but not on top.

physics_pretrain._comment: Self-supervised ball-dynamics pretraining, see agent_plans/ball_physics_pretrain_plan.md. Trains a small frozen encoder offline (train_ball_dynamics.py); the live network only ever loads its checkpoint via network.ball_physics_encoder_checkpoint below.

ball._comment_encoder_bottleneck_dim: Extra Linear+ReLU layer inserted between the encoder's hidden_dim trunk and the final Linear to latent_dim, so compression happens gradually (hidden_dim -> encoder_bottleneck_dim -> latent_dim) instead of jumping straight from hidden_dim to latent_dim in one step (e.g. 196->24 directly is an ~8x compression in a single Linear layer).
ball._comment_decoder_hidden_dim: Hidden layer size of the single shared decoder (latent + 3 horizon features [t_norm, t_norm^2, log1p(t)] -> decoder_hidden_dim -> ReLU -> 11 outputs), replacing the old one-independent-head-per-horizon design. Sharing weights across horizons lets the decoder generalize/interpolate the dynamics as a function of time instead of relearning similar physics per horizon; give it more capacity than the old per-head hidden size (32) since it now has to do the job for every horizon.
ball._comment_identity_shortcut_enabled: Hand-initializes an identity/passthrough path for the 9 raw pos/vel/spin fields on the encoder (concats x[0:9] onto the bottleneck output right before the final Linear to latent, weight-initialized so latent[0:9]~=x[0:9]) and, unless overridden by decoder_identity_shortcut_enabled below, on the decoder too (2 hidden ReLU units per value implement latent_i via ReLU(x)-ReLU(-x), ignoring the horizon features, so the decoder starts out predicting persistence at every horizon). See BallDynamicsEncoder/BallDynamicsDecoder docstrings in ball_dynamics_net.py. Everything still routes through the latent -- this only eases the encoder+decoder round trip (the post-training t=0 autoencoding sanity check) by giving training a much better starting point than random init, it doesn't bypass the latent the way a decoder-side skip around it would. Requires latent_dim >= 9. false (default) = plain random init, no behaviour change.
ball._comment_decoder_identity_shortcut_enabl: Overrides identity_shortcut_enabled for the DECODER only, so the encoder's concat+hand-init can stay on (e.g. to remain checkpoint-compatible with an encoder trained that way) while the decoder gets a plain random init with no hand-initialized persistence path -- and, just as importantly, none of _init_identity_shortcut_decoder's permanent gradient-masking protection on its dedicated units, so the decoder is free to move those weights away from the identity/persistence starting point if training finds something more useful, rather than being permanently walled off from ever repurposing them. null (default) = mirror identity_shortcut_enabled, the historical single-flag behaviour.
ball._comment_identity_shortcut_noise_std: Std of Gaussian noise added to the identity_shortcut's ~1/-1 weights at init, so the encoder+decoder round trip starts CLOSE to but not exactly at identity/persistence -- avoids exact weight-symmetry between the two hidden units backing each passthrough value, and means there's still something for training to learn rather than starting already perfect. Only used when identity_shortcut_enabled is true. 0.0 = exact identity init.
ball._comment_encoder_concat_all_input_fields: Requires identity_shortcut_enabled. Widens the encoder's identity-shortcut concat (see identity_shortcut_enabled's comment) from just the 9 pos/vel/spin fields to ALL N_INPUT_FIELDS (restitution, pitch/goal-dim ratios, the 6 engineered features too) -- gives the final latent-producing Linear direct, uncompressed access to everything, not just what `trunk`'s 3 ReLU layers manage to preserve. Cheap/safe to enable: that final layer has no ReLU of its own, so the newly-concatenated (zero-initialized) columns aren't a dead gradient fixed point -- ordinary gradient reaches them from the first backward pass, same as any normal zero-initialized Linear weight. false (default) = prior behaviour, only the 9 identity fields concatenated.
ball._comment_normalize_kinematics_by_base_pi: Controls which pitch scale position/velocity are normalized by in ball_episode_gen.py's _encode_input/_encode_target (dataset-generation time -- NOT a training-time flag, so changing this requires regenerating the dataset; existing .npz shards keep whatever convention they were built with, and nothing currently verifies a loaded dataset matches the CURRENT value of this flag, so keep it consistent across dataset-gen and training/diagnostics runs by hand). false (default, prior behaviour) = normalize pos/vel by EACH episode's own randomized pitch half_length/half_width/half_diag (pitch_scale_range above); position keeps 3 DIFFERENT per-axis divisors (half_length for x, half_width for y, the fixed height_norm_m for z), matching how it's always worked. Problem: two episodes with an IDENTICAL real-metres trajectory get DIFFERENT target values whenever their randomly-drawn pitch sizes differ, so the decoder has to implicitly recover each episode's pitch scale from the (unprotected, non-identity-shortcut) latent just to get the right output magnitude -- extra difficulty for the regression task that has nothing to do with predicting the actual physics. true = normalize pos/vel by the FIXED base/standard pitch dims instead, for every episode -- removes that implicit-recovery burden entirely (an identical real trajectory now gets an identical target regardless of that episode's pitch draw); position ALSO switches to ONE shared divisor (the fixed base pitch's half_diag) across all 3 axes x/y/height, matching velocity's convention, rather than height keeping its own much smaller height_norm_m scale (which would make height errors ~20x smaller in normalized space and barely register in pos_mse/pos_rmse). Cost: the pitch-boundary no longer sits at exactly |value|=1 (it's at the episode's own pitch_scale ratio instead, still available as an explicit, always-exact, never-through-the-bottleneck input feature -- see fields 10-13, unaffected by this flag either way). spin (ball_spin_norm_max_rad_s) normalization is always a fixed constant, not per-episode, so this flag doesn't touch it.
ball._comment_goal_net_collisions_enabled: Dataset-generation-time flag (like normalize_kinematics_by_base_pitch above -- NOT a training-time switch, changing this requires regenerating the dataset). true (default, prior behaviour) = resolve_goal_boundary() runs every tick once the ball has passed the goal line, bouncing it off the back net/side posts/crossbar like real goal-frame physics. false = skip that call entirely -- the ball just keeps flying through the goal mouth under regular gravity/drag/Magnus/ground-bounce physics (step_ball only), as if the net/posts/crossbar weren't there. Useful for isolating whether the goal-frame bounce geometry (a small, high-curvature region of state space -- similar bounce-timing sensitivity to pitch-boundary bounces) is a meaningful contributor to the mid-horizon error spike, independent of whatever's happening with regular pitch-boundary out-of-bounds bounces.
ball._comment_spin_active_frac: Fraction of episodes given a random-axis, random-magnitude spin (§4.2). The rest get zero spin -- real play is usually low/no-spin, so always sampling nonzero spin would over-represent it in the training distribution.
ball._comment_freeze_semantics: TRAINING-time choice (unlike normalize_kinematics_by_base_pitch above) of which out_of_bounds/goal_scored convention to train against -- the dataset itself always stores BOTH: the always-continuous physics trajectory (ball_episode_gen.py no longer freezes/stops early on either event -- goal-net/post/crossbar bounce physics and regular gravity/drag/Magnus/ground-bounce physics keep running the whole horizon regardless, so a ball can genuinely bounce back into bounds or back out of a goal mouth) AND, per episode, the full state at the moment out_of_bounds/goal_scored FIRST became true (`crossings`/`crossing_times` in each .npz shard). true (default, prior behaviour) = BallDynamicsDataset.targets_with_freeze_semantics() reconstructs the OLD semantics before training starts: state frozen at the first crossing, held (and both flags latched true) for every later horizon. false = train against the raw stored data as-is -- physics never freezes, and out_of_bounds/goal_scored at each horizon are INSTANTANEOUS (can legitimately un-set again at a later horizon if the ball bounces back in/out). Since both conventions live in the same generated dataset, comparing them is just flipping this flag and re-running -- no regeneration needed.
ball._comment_weight_decay: L2 weight decay for the MAIN LOOP's optimizer ONLY (torch.optim.Adam(..., weight_decay=...)) -- NOT applied to autoencode_optimizer or decoder_only_optimizer. Motivated by a persistent train/val generalization gap observed in real runs (val pos/vel/spin RMSE + R^2 consistently worse than train, not shrinking even late in a cosine cycle when per-epoch weight movement is small -- see physics_runs.md and agent_plans/ball_physics_pretrain_plan.md 12.6). Scoping caveat: uniform decay pulls EVERY parameter toward 0 every step, including the identity-shortcut's hand-set weights -- decay is NOT blocked by the identity-shortcut's backward-hook gradient masks (those only zero gradients from the LOSS, not the optimizer's separate decay term). The main loop's own t=0 term (autoencode_during_main_loop_enabled) runs every epoch specifically to pull those weights back toward exact, so a small value should settle into a mild equilibrium rather than eroding away -- watch train_t0/val_t0 pos/vel/spin RMSE in the logs to confirm it's holding if trying a larger value. 0.0 (default) = disabled, no behaviour change. Try 1e-5 to 1e-4 as a starting point.
ball._comment_optimizer_type: Which optimizer drives the MAIN LOOP -- autoencode_optimizer_type/decoder_only_optimizer_type (see the autoencode-pretrain/decoder-only-pretrain groups below) control their own phases independently (they used to always be forced to Adam regardless of this value; now each phase can be tuned separately, though 'adam' remains the sensible default for those early warmup phases). 'adam' (default, no behaviour change): per-parameter adaptive step size (lr / sqrt(recent grad variance)) -- fast and robust early on, but that same adaptivity means a parameter with quiet recent gradients can get a disproportionately LARGE effective step the moment a slightly bigger gradient shows up, even at a tiny nominal lr -- a plausible source of occasional worse-epoch val_loss bumps late in an already-converging run. 'sgd': plain (optionally momentum, see sgd_momentum) SGD -- step is just lr*grad, no per-parameter denominator to spike, typically smoother/more monotonic once already near a good minimum. Meant for resuming a late-stage run via --init-checkpoint to compare against continuing under Adam, not as a from-scratch default -- SGD usually needs its own (often larger) lr re-tuned rather than reusing whatever worked for Adam.
ball._comment_sgd_momentum: Momentum for the main-loop optimizer when optimizer_type='sgd' (torch.optim.SGD(..., momentum=...)) -- ignored when optimizer_type='adam'. 0.9 is the conventional default for SGD+momentum; 0.0 = plain vanilla SGD with no momentum term at all.
ball._comment_lr_cosine: Cosine annealing with warm restarts (SGDR): LR decays smoothly from `lr` to `lr * lr_cosine_eta_min_frac` over lr_cosine_restart_epochs epochs, then jumps back up and repeats (each cycle lr_cosine_t_mult times longer than the last -- 2.0 = 15, 30, 60, ... epoch cycles). Helps when train loss oscillates-but-occasionally-improves late in training (LR too coarse for the local curvature near the minimum) by letting it actually settle within each cycle, while the restarts still give it a chance to escape a bad spot. lr_cosine_peak_decay multiplies the RESTART peak itself by this factor every cycle (0.85 = each restart peaks 15% lower than the last) -- PyTorch's scheduler has no built-in option for this (vanilla SGDR always restarts to the same peak forever), so it's applied manually in train_ball_dynamics.py. 1.0 = no peak decay. Set lr_cosine_restart_epochs to null or 0 to disable cosine restarts entirely (flat LR for the whole run, prior behaviour). NOTE: lr_cosine_t_mult must resolve to an integer -- PyTorch's CosineAnnealingWarmRestarts requires int T_mult, so this is truncated via int(), e.g. 1.5 currently truncates to 1 (no cycle growth) -- see train() call site if you actually want fractional cycle growth (would need a custom scheduler).
ball._comment_pos_weight_max: Caps the auto-computed inverse-frequency pos_weight (out_of_bounds/goal_scored, per horizon) before use in the BCE loss -- null = uncapped. Same convention as bc.pos_weight_max. Set a float if a horizon's rare-event weight gets large enough to destabilise training (goal_scored is the more likely candidate, being the rarer of the two flags).
ball._comment_bce_loss_weight: Multiplies the oob_scored/goal_scored BCE terms' contribution to every backpropagated loss in this run (main per-horizon heads, adjacent-pair, autoencode-pretrain, the t0 term -- everywhere compute_loss/_single_target_loss(_with_breakdown) is called). Reported oob_bce/goal_bce metrics in the logs are ALWAYS the raw, unweighted value regardless of this setting, so runs with different weights stay directly comparable. 1.0 (default) = no behaviour change. 0.0 fully disables the classification heads' gradient -- pos/vel/spin regression trains exactly as if out_of_bounds/goal_scored didn't exist as targets at all, useful for testing whether the classification heads are competing with (dragging down) regression quality. When 0.0, oob_bce/goal_bce are also skipped from the per-epoch diagnostic printout (nothing to watch, since they never move).
ball._comment_spin_loss_weight: Same idea as bce_loss_weight but for the spin MSE term -- multiplies spin's contribution to every backpropagated loss (same call sites). Reported spin_rmse is ALWAYS the raw, unweighted value regardless of this setting. 1.0 (default) = no behaviour change. 0.0 fully disables the spin head's gradient, useful for testing whether spin regression is competing with (dragging down) pos/vel quality. When 0.0, spin_rmse is also skipped from the per-epoch diagnostic printout.
ball._comment_crossing_loss_weight: Multiplies model.crossing_head's own loss (a Linear(latent_dim, 3) reading directly off the latent, no hidden layer -- predicts the ball's out-of-bounds/goal-scored crossing position (pos_x, pos_y ONLY, no height) and delta_t (seconds until that crossing, -1 sentinel if it never happens within the simulated window), as ONE global per-episode prediction rather than per-horizon) -- see BallDynamicsAutoencoder's docstring and BallDynamicsDataset.crossing_pos/crossing_dt/crossing_mask. Position loss is masked to episodes that actually crossed; delta_t loss is unmasked, trained directly against the -1 sentinel. 1.0 (default) = fully trained alongside everything else. 0.0 fully disables its gradient -- the head still exists in every checkpoint (so shapes stay stable across runs with different weights) but never gets supervision, equivalent to not having built it at all.
ball._comment_resting_loss_weight: Multiplies model.resting_head's own loss (a Linear(latent_dim, 2) reading directly off the latent, no hidden layer -- predicts where the ball FINALLY comes to rest, pos_x/pos_y only, as ONE global per-episode prediction) -- see BallDynamicsAutoencoder's docstring and BallDynamicsDataset.compute_resting_targets. Unlike crossing_head, resting targets are derivable from inputs/targets alone (no extra recorded dataset columns needed) but are only DEFINED for episodes that (a) start faster than resting_min_start_speed_mps and (b) actually drop below resting_speed_threshold_mps at some recorded horizon -- episodes failing either are excluded from this loss entirely (no sentinel, unlike crossing's delta_t). 1.0 (default) = fully trained. 0.0 fully disables its gradient -- the head still exists in every checkpoint but never gets supervision.
ball._comment_resting_min_start_speed_mps: Minimum ball speed (real m/s) at t=0 for an episode to be eligible for the resting-position target -- an already-slow ball makes 'predict where it stops' close to a trivial 'same place it started' answer. Converted to normalized units via pitch_half_diag_m, same approximation used for adjacent_pair_min_start_speed_mps.
ball._comment_resting_speed_threshold_mps: Speed (real m/s) below which the ball counts as 'at rest' at a given recorded horizon -- among an eligible episode's horizons that drop below this, the LATEST one's (pos_x, pos_y) becomes the resting-position target (latest rather than first, since the ball may still be settling -- bouncing/rolling -- at an earlier low-speed instant). Episodes that never drop below this within the recorded horizons are excluded from the loss entirely. Converted to normalized units via pitch_half_diag_m, same convention as resting_min_start_speed_mps.
ball._comment_adjacent_pair_training_enabled: Adds extra (input, target) training pairs derived from data already fully recorded, no new simulation needed: treats each recorded horizon's state as a new pseudo-initial-state, predicting the NEXT recorded horizon from it via a fixed, statically-known delta (BallDynamicsDataset.build_adjacent_pair_data()). Exposes the encoder to more realistic 'mid-trajectory' input states, not just the original uniform-random t=0 sampling -- relevant for the eventual live-deployment encoder (§8), which will see whatever state the ball happens to be in mid-match. Episodes already resolved (out_of_bounds/goal_scored) by the pair's start horizon are excluded (predicting 'stays frozen' is trivially correct and would dilute the signal). Set false to disable without touching anything else.
ball._comment_adjacent_pair_max_skip: How many horizons AHEAD of each start horizon to also predict, not just the immediately-next one. 1 (default) is strictly adjacent (prior behaviour); 2 or 3 additionally trains 'skip one/two horizons ahead' pairs from the same pseudo-starts. Every skip from the same start horizon shares ONE encoder pass (see build_adjacent_pair_data's docstring) -- costs one extra forward_at() decode per skip, not a full extra encoder call, same 'one encoder pass, several decoder queries, summed loss' pattern the main per-horizon task already uses. Deliberately not swept all the way to ALL (i, j) pairs: the shared decoder's continuous horizon features (t_norm, t_norm^2, log1p(t)) already generalize across arbitrary deltas, so long-range pairs mostly retest what the main task + short pairs already cover, while full all-pairs would be a combinatorially large row count for a large horizon list.
ball._comment_adjacent_pair_min_start_speed_m: Minimum ball speed (real m/s) at a pair's START horizon for that row to be included. 0.0 (default) keeps every row (prior behaviour). A near-stationary ball (already resting/rolling to a near-stop) makes 'predict approximately no further movement' a near-trivial target, same rationale as excluding already-resolved starts. Converted to normalized units internally via pitch_half_diag_m (the same approximate real-unit stand-in scale used elsewhere in train_ball_dynamics.py) -- exact when normalize_kinematics_by_base_pitch is true, an approximation otherwise.
ball._comment_autoencode_pretrain_epochs: Number of epochs to spend BEFORE the main training loop purely autoencoding: for every recorded horizon (not just t=0), treat its recorded state as a pseudo-initial-state and train the encoder+decoder to reconstruct it via decoder.forward_at(latent, 0.0) -- see BallDynamicsDataset.build_autoencoding_data(). Primes the encoder+decoder to round-trip through the latent bottleneck before also asking them to learn dynamics; complements (doesn't replace) the post-training t=0 sanity check that's always logged. 0 (default) = disabled, no behaviour change. Flat LR (main lr, no cosine schedule) during this phase.
ball._comment_autoencode_lr: Learning rate used ONLY during autoencode pretraining (physics_pretrain.ball.autoencode_pretrain_epochs), via its own Adam instance -- separate from `lr` (the main dynamics-training loop's peak LR, subject to the cosine schedule below) so the two phases can be tuned independently instead of sharing one flat rate. Sensible to differ: autoencoding is a much easier task (copy-through via forward_at(latent, 0.0), no real dynamics to learn) than the main loop's multi-horizon dynamics prediction, so the right step size isn't necessarily the same. Falls back to `lr` if unset. Always flat (no cosine schedule) -- that's tuned for the main loop specifically.
ball._comment_autoencode_optimizer_type: Which optimizer drives autoencode pretraining (physics_pretrain.ball.autoencode_pretrain_epochs) -- independent of the main loop's optimizer_type above. Same 'adam'/'sgd' semantics (see optimizer_type's comment for the tradeoff); 'adam' (default, prior behaviour -- this phase used to always be Adam regardless of optimizer_type) is normally right for this fast early-warmup phase, but nothing stops trying 'sgd' if it shows the same late-stage-noise symptom optimizer_type was added for.
ball._comment_autoencode_sgd_momentum: Momentum for the autoencode-pretrain optimizer when autoencode_optimizer_type='sgd' (torch.optim.SGD(..., momentum=...)) -- ignored when 'adam'. Same convention as sgd_momentum.
ball._comment_autoencode_during_main_loop_ena: Keeps a small t=0 reconstruction term (same mechanism as autoencode_pretrain_epochs -- decoder.forward_at(latent, 0.0) on every recorded horizon's state, reused for free) running as an extra pass EVERY epoch of the MAIN loop too, not just before it. Without this, nothing supervises t=0 once the main loop starts (horizons_s never includes a literal 0.0), so main-loop gradients driven purely by the 0.2s-10.0s targets are free to erode whatever t=0 quality autoencode pretraining established, with zero corrective signal until the post-training t=0 diagnostic reports the damage after the fact. Logged as train_t0_loss/val_t0_loss, saved to .history.npz. true (default) = enabled, since the data is already derived for free (pure reshaping, no new simulation) regardless of this flag's value if autoencode_pretrain_epochs > 0 too.
ball._comment_decoder_only_pretrain_epochs: Number of epochs to spend AFTER autoencode pretraining but BEFORE the main joint loop, training the decoder plus the encoder's latent-producing layer (encoder.out) on the REAL per-horizon dynamics task -- same training the main loop does (main per-horizon loss + adjacent-pair + t=0 term), just without letting the decoder's initially-large, far-from-converged dynamics loss drag the encoder's EARLIER layers (encoder.trunk, frozen this phase) around (same failure class as the classification leak fixed via BallDynamicsDecoder's identity-shortcut masks, one level further out: a freshly-initialized head's big gradient corrupting an already-good backbone on epoch 1 of joint training). encoder.out itself IS trainable here (unlike the older full-encoder-freeze this replaced) so the latent's non-identity 'spare' dims can start shaping themselves toward dynamics-useful features a whole phase earlier instead of sitting untouched until the main loop -- but encoder.out's IDENTITY rows (producing latent[0:N_IDENTITY_SHORTCUT_FIELDS] ~= raw pos/vel/spin) are gradient-masked for the duration of this phase specifically (register_hook, same 'no soft version of this' precedent as the decoder's own identity-shortcut masking), since this phase's decoder is at its freshest/noisiest and exposing those rows to it directly would reopen the same corruption risk one layer further upstream. The mask is removed again before the main loop, which trains encoder.out fully unmasked as it always has. Full diagnostic logging (matches a regular main-loop epoch), but NOT persisted to history/.history.npz/report.html -- this is a deliberately short warm-up, not a run of its own. No LR schedule here, same convention as autoencode_pretrain_epochs -- but DOES track the best-val-loss epoch's weights and restore them at the end of this phase (unconditionally, not just on stagnation), so a bad final epoch (this phase's LR is flat and can be noisy -- val_loss spikes of 2-5x the typical level between good epochs are common) doesn't silently hand a worse-than-necessary starting point to the main loop. See decoder_only_early_stop_patience below for optionally cutting this phase short once val stops improving. 0 (default) = disabled, no behaviour change.
ball._comment_decoder_only_pretrain_lr: Learning rate used ONLY during decoder-only pretraining, via its own Adam instance (built over decoder parameters only). Falls back to `lr` if unset. Always flat, no cosine schedule.
ball._comment_decoder_only_optimizer_type: Which optimizer drives decoder-only pretraining (physics_pretrain.ball.decoder_only_pretrain_epochs) -- independent of the main loop's optimizer_type above. Same 'adam'/'sgd' semantics (see optimizer_type's comment); 'adam' (default, prior behaviour -- this phase used to always be Adam regardless of optimizer_type) is normally right for this phase.
ball._comment_decoder_only_sgd_momentum: Momentum for the decoder-only-pretrain optimizer when decoder_only_optimizer_type='sgd' -- ignored when 'adam'. Same convention as sgd_momentum.
ball._comment_decoder_only_early_stop_patienc: Early stopping for the decoder-only-pretrain phase specifically -- separate from early_stop_patience/early_stop_min_delta below, which only govern the MAIN loop. Best-val weight tracking/restore always happens regardless of this setting (see decoder_only_pretrain_epochs above); this only adds an early BREAK out of that phase's epoch loop once val_loss hasn't improved by more than decoder_only_early_stop_min_delta for this many consecutive epochs, so a decoder_only_pretrain_epochs budget that's mostly wasted after convergence doesn't have to be shortened by hand. 0 (default) = disabled, always runs the full configured epoch count, no behaviour change.
ball._comment_decoder_only_early_stop_min_del: Minimum val_loss improvement (over the best seen so far in THIS phase) to reset decoder_only_early_stop_patience's counter and count as 'improved' rather than 'stagnant'. Only has any effect when decoder_only_early_stop_patience > 0.
ball._comment_decoder_only_pretrain_freeze_la: Whether encoder.out (the latent-producing layer) stays frozen during decoder-only pretraining, or is left trainable. false (default, no behaviour change) = only encoder.trunk is frozen; encoder.out trains too (added to decoder_only_optimizer), with its identity rows gradient-masked (register_hook) so the decoder's freshest/noisiest gradient this phase can't corrupt the identity-shortcut mapping -- lets the latent's non-identity 'spare' dims start shaping themselves toward dynamics-useful features a whole phase earlier instead of sitting untouched until the main loop. true = the ENTIRE encoder (trunk AND encoder.out) is frozen for this phase, matching this pipeline's ORIGINAL (pre-identity-row-masking) behaviour -- the decoder trains purely against whatever latent the encoder already produces, zero risk of this phase's gradient touching the encoder at all, but the latent sits completely inert through the whole phase. For A/B-testing whether letting the latent move here actually helps, not a strictly-better default either way.

player._comment: Self-supervised player-dynamics pretraining, see agent_plans/player_physics_pretrain_plan.md. Mirrors physics_pretrain.ball's structure/naming convention -- see that section's own comments for anything not re-explained here. Trains a small frozen encoder offline (train_player_dynamics.py); no live-network wiring exists yet (out of scope for this pass, see the plan doc).
player._comment_encoder_bottleneck_dim: Same rationale as physics_pretrain.ball.encoder_bottleneck_dim -- gradual compression (hidden_dim -> encoder_bottleneck_dim -> latent_dim) instead of one big jump.
player._comment_decoder_hidden_dim: Hidden layer size of the single shared decoder (latent + 3 horizon features -> decoder_hidden_dim -> ReLU -> N_TARGET_FIELDS_PER_HORIZON=9 outputs). Same convention as physics_pretrain.ball.decoder_hidden_dim.
player._comment_autoencode_pretrain_epochs: Epochs to spend BEFORE the main loop purely autoencoding (t=0 reconstruction of every recorded horizon's own state via decoder.forward_at(latent, 0.0)) -- see physics_pretrain.ball's identical key. 0 (default) = disabled.
player._comment_autoencode_lr: LR used only during autoencode pretraining, own Adam instance. Falls back to `lr` if unset.
player._comment_autoencode_during_main_loop_ena: Keeps a small t=0 reconstruction term running every epoch of the MAIN loop too (interleaved with the main per-horizon pass and adjacent-pair pass, NOT a separate sequential phase -- see train_player_dynamics.py's _run_interleaved_train_epoch). true (default) = enabled.
player._comment_decoder_only_pretrain_epochs: Epochs to spend AFTER autoencode pretraining but BEFORE the main joint loop, training the decoder (plus optionally encoder.out) against the real per-horizon dynamics task while encoder.trunk stays frozen -- see physics_pretrain.ball's identical key for the full rationale. 0 (default) = disabled.
player._comment_decoder_only_pretrain_lr: LR used only during decoder-only pretraining, own Adam instance. Falls back to `lr` if unset.
player._comment_decoder_only_early_stop: Early stopping for the decoder-only-pretrain phase specifically, separate from early_stop_patience/early_stop_min_delta below (which only govern the MAIN loop). 0 patience = disabled, always runs the full configured epoch count.
player._comment_decoder_only_pretrain_freeze_la: true (default) = the ENTIRE encoder (trunk AND encoder.out) is frozen for this phase -- the decoder trains purely against whatever latent the encoder already produces. false = only encoder.trunk is frozen; encoder.out trains too, with its identity rows gradient-masked so the decoder's freshest/noisiest gradient can't corrupt the identity-shortcut mapping. See physics_pretrain.ball's identical key for the full A/B-testing rationale.
player._comment_adjacent_pair_training_enabled: Adds extra pair-training targets derived from data already fully recorded: treats each recorded horizon's state as a new pseudo-initial-state, predicting later recorded horizons from it (see train_player_dynamics.py's _build_horizon_bundle/_run_interleaved_train_epoch 'horizon' branch) -- exposes the encoder to more realistic 'mid-trajectory' input states. UNLIKE the ball version, there is no resolved-state row filter here by default (see adjacent_pair_min_start_speed_mps below for the one optional exclusion) -- the player pipeline has no freeze-on-event rule, so every row is an equally legitimate pair. Rides the SAME shared rows/encoder pass as the t0 autoencode task (see autoencode_during_main_loop_enabled) rather than its own separate batches. Set false to disable.
player._comment_adjacent_pair_max_skip: How many horizons AHEAD of each start horizon to also predict, not just the immediately-next one. 1 (default) is strictly adjacent. Every skip from the same start horizon shares ONE encoder pass -- costs one extra forward_at() decode per skip, not a full extra encoder call, same 'one encoder pass, several decoder queries, summed loss' pattern the main per-horizon task already uses. See physics_pretrain.ball.adjacent_pair_max_skip's identical key for the full rationale (why this isn't swept to ALL (i, j) pairs).
player._comment_adjacent_pair_min_start_speed_m: Minimum player speed (real m/s) at a pair's START horizon for that row to be mask-eligible for pair training. 0.0 (default) keeps every row. A near-stationary player makes 'predict approximately no movement' a near-trivial target for pair training, same rationale as physics_pretrain.ball.adjacent_pair_min_start_speed_mps. Converted to normalized units internally via pitch_half_diag_m (the same approximate real-unit stand-in scale used elsewhere in train_player_dynamics.py) -- exact when normalize_kinematics_by_base_pitch is true, an approximation otherwise.
player._comment_identity_shortcut_enabled: Hand-initializes an identity/passthrough path for the 7 raw pos/vel/heading/stamina fields on the encoder and (unless overridden by decoder_identity_shortcut_enabled below) the decoder too -- see PlayerDynamicsEncoder/PlayerDynamicsDecoder docstrings. Requires latent_dim >= 7. false = plain random init, no behaviour change.
player._comment_decoder_identity_shortcut_enabl: Overrides identity_shortcut_enabled for the DECODER only -- see physics_pretrain.ball's identical key. null (default) = mirror identity_shortcut_enabled.
player._comment_identity_shortcut_noise_std: Std of Gaussian noise added to the identity_shortcut's ~1/-1 weights at init -- see physics_pretrain.ball's identical key. 0.0 = exact identity init.
player._comment_encoder_concat_all_input_fields: Requires identity_shortcut_enabled. Widens the encoder's identity-shortcut concat from just the 7 pos/vel/heading/stamina fields to ALL N_INPUT_FIELDS (attrs, has_possession, desired_direction/speed_mode, pitch/goal dims, engineered features too). false (default) = only the 7 identity fields concatenated.
player._comment_horizons_s: The 5 fixed decoder-head horizons (seconds), matching the original design sketch in agent_plans/ball_physics_pretrain_plan.md section 11. sim_dt_s (observation.sim_dt_s) must evenly divide each of these for exact horizon alignment (see player_episode_gen.generate_episode's docstring).
player._comment_pitch_scale_range: Per-episode randomization range for pitch/goal dims, as a multiplier on the base/standard dims -- same convention as physics_pretrain.ball.pitch_scale_range.
player._comment_normalize_kinematics_by_base_pi: Controls which pitch scale position/velocity are normalized by in player_episode_gen.py's _encode_input/_encode_target (dataset-generation time -- NOT a training-time flag, changing this requires regenerating the dataset). false = normalize pos/vel by EACH episode's own randomized pitch half_length/half_width/half_diag. true (default) = normalize by the FIXED base/standard pitch dims instead, removing the implicit per-episode-scale-recovery burden from the decoder -- see physics_pretrain.ball.normalize_kinematics_by_base_pitch's much longer comment for the full rationale (identical here, minus the height/z special-case, which doesn't apply to a grounded player).
player._comment_out_of_bounds_start_frac: Fraction of episodes whose player starts already out of pitch bounds (see player_episode_gen._sample_position_already_special) -- same convention as physics_pretrain.ball.out_of_bounds_start_frac.
player._comment_possession_start_frac: Fraction of episodes where this player starts (and stays, for the whole episode -- fixed, not re-rolled per tick) in possession of the ball (has_possession=1), driving both effective_top_speed's ball_carry_speed_multiplier and whether goal_scored is ever physically meaningful for this episode (always 0 when has_possession=0 -- see player_episode_gen.generate_episode's docstring).
player._comment_intent_continue_prob: Probability, at each intent resample point (t=0 excluded -- always fresh there), of CONTINUING the previous intent (same speed_mode, direction perturbed by intent_continue_heading_jitter_std_rad) rather than drawing an entirely fresh direction+speed_mode. Default 0.5 = 'about half the time continue in a straight line or almost', per the design brief.
player._comment_intent_continue_heading_jitter_: Std (radians) of the Gaussian jitter applied to the previous direction when 'continuing' an intent (see intent_continue_prob) -- 0.15 rad ~= 8.6 degrees, a small wobble, not a sharp turn.
player._comment_speed_mode_weights: Categorical weights [w_standstill, w_jog, w_sprint] for a FRESH intent draw (see player_episode_gen._sample_speed_mode) -- need not sum to 1, normalized internally.
player._comment_weight_decay: L2 weight decay for the MAIN LOOP's optimizer only -- see physics_pretrain.ball.weight_decay's much longer comment for the full rationale (identical here).
player._comment_optimizer_type: Which optimizer drives the MAIN LOOP ONLY -- autoencode_optimizer/decoder_only_optimizer always stay Adam regardless of this. See physics_pretrain.ball.optimizer_type's much longer comment for the full rationale (identical here). 'adam' (default, no behaviour change) for from-scratch training; 'sgd' (see sgd_momentum) for smoother late-stage fine-convergence, typically when resuming a late-stage run via --init-checkpoint -- needs its own (often larger) lr re-tuned rather than reusing whatever worked for Adam.
player._comment_sgd_momentum: Momentum for the main-loop optimizer when optimizer_type='sgd' (torch.optim.SGD(..., momentum=...)) -- ignored when optimizer_type='adam'. 0.9 is the conventional default for SGD+momentum; 0.0 = plain vanilla SGD with no momentum term at all.
player._comment_bce_loss_weight: Multiplies the out_of_bounds/goal_scored BCE terms' contribution to every backpropagated loss in this run -- see physics_pretrain.ball.bce_loss_weight's identical key. 0.0 fully disables the classification heads' gradient (and skips them from the per-epoch diagnostic printout).
player._comment_pos_weight_max: Caps the auto-computed inverse-frequency pos_weight (out_of_bounds/goal_scored, per horizon) before use in the BCE loss -- null = uncapped. goal_scored's pos_weight is computed ONLY over has_possession=1 rows (see PlayerDynamicsDataset.compute_pos_weights), since a non-possessing row's goal_scored is always a physically meaningless 0 -- including those rows in the class-balance computation would inflate the weight past what the meaningful subset actually needs.
